title: "As is his desire, so is his will; as his will, so his deed" (4.4)
hook: January's gym crowd thins out by March, and a line from the Upanishad looks one step further back
tomorrow: neti, neti — the great unborn self

segments.voice: Yesterday: death, pictured as a caterpillar reaching the next blade before it lets go. Your line was the leaf.

In January, the gym fills up: new shoes, new plans, a firm decision. By March, a lot of the new faces are gone. It usually isn't for lack of information; plenty of them knew what to do. They made a resolution, and it didn't hold. Yajnavalkya, still talking with King Janaka about what happens after death, stops to explain where a life actually comes from, and it's one step further back than the January crowd starts.
screen: `JANUARY: THE GYM IS FULL.` → `MARCH: IT'S EMPTY.` → `ONE STEP FURTHER BACK.`

segments.voice: As a person acts, he says, as a person behaves, so they become. Doing good, one becomes good. Doing harm, one becomes harmful. That's the karma Artabhaga heard about in private, now said out loud to a king. But then he goes deeper. Some say, he adds, a person is made of desire. And here's the line: yathakamo bhavati tat kratur bhavati. As is the desire, so is the will. As is the will, so is the deed. As is the deed, so is what one becomes. Four steps. Desire, the wanting underneath. Kratu, the will or resolve, the decision you make. The deed, the thing you actually do. And what you reach, what you turn into. The January crowd starts at step two, the resolution, and wonders why it doesn't hold. The text says the resolution grows out of what you actually want. Then Yajnavalkya follows it past death. The one who still desires goes on, carried by the deed to what the mind clung to, and when that's spent, comes back to act again. But the one who doesn't desire, whose only desire is the self, doesn't wander. And then a verse the Katha Upanishad shares: when all the desires that live in the heart are let go, the mortal becomes immortal, and reaches Brahman, here. And the body? It lies like a snake's old skin on an anthill, dead and cast off.
screen: `AS ONE ACTS, SO ONE BECOMES.` · `A PERSON IS MADE OF DESIRE.` · `DESIRE, WILL, DEED, WHAT YOU REACH.` · `THE SNAKE'S OLD SKIN.` · then, large: `DESIRE → WILL → DEED → DESTINY.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you did today, small or large, and ask what you decided that made you do it. Then go one step further, to what you wanted underneath the decision. Don't judge the want; just find it, and let it be seen.
Kratu, will, resolve, purpose. The step between what you want and what you do: as the desire, so the kratu.
Your line: desire, will, deed, destiny. In this verse, the wanting comes first. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindu teachers cite this verse to explain karma as growing from desire and intention, not only from outward acts; the line about letting go of the heart's desires (4.4.7) also appears in the Katha Upanishad.

fork.setup: you've made a firm resolution three times and it never holds. according to this verse, where should you look?
options: at what you actually desire, underneath it.
fork.reveal: as is the desire, so is the will. the resolution grows out of the wanting, so the text sends you one step further back.

original.note: Sanskrit kratu: will, resolve, purpose. yathākāmo bhavati tat kratur bhavati (4.4.5).

trapdoor: what you thought: you are what you do.
what it means: you become what you do, you do what you will, and you will what you desire. it starts with the wanting.
what a scholar hears: 4.4.5 moves karma from ritual act to inner desire (kāma) and resolve (kratu); 4.4.7 is shared with Katha Upanishad 2.3.14.
guess: will, resolve: the step between wanting and doing
the deed itself, the thing you actually do
a desire buried deep in the heart

chat.says: Why do my New Year's resolutions never seem to stick?

chat.meaning: Yathakamo bhavati tat kratur bhavati: as is the desire, so is the will; as the will, so the deed; as the deed, so one becomes.

karma.meaning: action, and what it makes of the one who acts

notes: The index word is the title's head cut at the comma ("As is his desire); kept exactly.
4.4.5 paraphrased; Sanskrit quoted without diacritics (yathākāmo bhavati tat kratur bhavati). Confirm.
Snake-slough simile: 4.4.7. Katha parallel numbered 2.3.14 (or 6.14). Confirm.
The popular modern rendering ('You are what your deep, driving desire is…') is not named or quoted; the script only says it is modern and loose.
